item.title: The chemistry of the interstellar medium
item.description:
The interstellar medium#

In all galaxies, the space between celestial bodies is filled with a collection of gas and dust particles. These particles are known as interstellar medium (ISM) and possesses density of $10^{-9}$ grains$\times$cm$^{-3}$. [1] The ISM is a reservoir of constituents for the formation of new stars. It is mostly composed of hydrogen atoms, the second most common element is helium with a relative abundance of 8.5$\times 10^{-2}$ per hydrogen atom, followed by oxygen (2.6$\times 10^{-4}$per hydrogen atom [2] ) and carbon (1.2$\times 10^{-4}$ [3] per hydrogen atom). All other elements are present with abundances lower than $10^{-4}$.
